Another reason is that the damage increases the production of insulin, which keeps moving glucose into storage, even when the blood glucose level is low.","A review of 15 longitudinal studies found that depression increased the probability of obesity, and that obesity increased the probability of depression, but both effects were small.","One study found obesity in 19 percent of people with a history of depression and in 15 percent of those who had","Another study found that the average adult with depression gained about a pound per year, whereas the average for everyone else was about 8/10 of a pound. Many studies have found that the children of obese mothers are more likely than average to become obese themselves.","Researchers using laboratory animals randomly assigned pregnant females to a control diet or a diet that produces obesity.","Studies of twins and adopted children in many countries have consistently found high heritability of body weight.","For example, Prader-Willi syndrome is marked by mild cognitive disabilities, short stature, and obesity, with of course variation among individuals.","A second type, monogenic obesity, occurs when a single gene causes obesity without other physical or mental abnormalities. The most common type of monogenetic obesity comes from a mutation in the gene for the melanocortin receptor (important for satiety).","Researchers have identified many other genetic variants that increase or decrease the probability of obesity.","However, obesity was uncommon among them in the early 1900s, when their diet consisted mostly of desert plants that ripen in the brief rainy season. The Pima apparently evolved a strategy of eating all they could when food was available, because it would have to carry them through periods of scarcity.","That statement may be true, but it means little unless we know how long they kept the weight off, or how many other people tried the plan and failed to lose weight.","Exercise is important, and it need not be strenuous, but it needs to be consistent, such as a long brisk walk on most days.","A study found that fourteen such supplements contain oxilofrine, a stimulant never approved by the Food and Drug Administration. A placebo-controlled study found that combining semaglutide with a program of exercise and a low-calorie diet led to a mean loss of 16 percent of body weight, with side effects that most people found tolerable.","Recall that glucagon is a pancreatic hormone that increases the release of glucose into the blood.","As Figure 9.21 shows, GLP-1 increases activity in the satiety areas of the hypothalamus.","Here is still another option, experimental and controversial: People’s digestive systems have microorganisms that help digest the foods and perform many other functions, some helpful to us and some harmful. Small-sample experiments with both mice and humans have shown that transferring intestinal microorganisms from lean to overweight individuals produces at least temporary benefits.","Bulimia nervosa is a condition in which people alternate between strict dieting and binges of overeating.","In the United States, the prevalence of bulimia is about 1 percent of women and 0.1 percent of men (Hoek","Bulimia nervosa has been recorded only in cultures with a strong western influence, and cases are known where it began to occur after the introduction of American movies and television programs. On average, people with bulimia show a variety of biochemical abnormalities, including increased production of ghrelin, a hormone associated with increased appetite.","After therapy that decreases the symptoms of bulimia, the body chemicals return toward normal levels.","Eating tasty foods activates the same brain areas as addictive drugs, such as the nucleus accumbens. Over several weeks on this regimen, the rats drank more and more each day, especially during the first hour of availability each day.","Anorexia nervosa is characterized by a refusal to eat enough to maintain a healthy body weight.","Because the condition varies in severity, estimates of prevalence also vary, depending on the diagnostic criteria.","However, the research agrees that anorexia is much more common among females than males, and that the onset is usually in the teenage years.","Contrary to what we might expect of people verging on starvation, those with anorexia generally engage in vigorous physical activity. The American Psychiatric Association lists anorexia nervosa as a mental disorder, but depending on the definition of mental disorder, not everyone agrees.","Although most people with anorexia experience some degree of anxiety or depression, few people had a noticeable disorder before the anorexia.","Brain research has found abnormalities of dopamine release in anorexia, but the brain abnormalities are more likely a result of weight loss than a cause. However, the complexity of the system also provides a kind of security: If one part of the system makes a mistake, another part can counteract it.","The regulation of eating succeeds not in spite of its complexity but because of it.","The ability to digest a food is one major determinant of preference for that food. For example, people who cannot digest lactose generally do not like to eat dairy products.","Widespread beliefs that sugar causes hyperactivity and that turkey causes sleepiness are unfounded. However, research does support the idea that eating fish is good for brain functioning. People and animals eat partly for the sake of taste. However, a sham-feeding animal, which tastes its foods but does not absorb them, eats almost constantly. Taste is not sufficient to satisfy hunger.","In addition to taste, other factors controlling hunger include distension of the stomach and intestines, secretion of CCK by the duodenum, and the availability of glucose and other nutrients to the cells."],"classroomResearch":{"title":"Evidence in context: The Stomach and Intestines","body":"In a decisive experiment, researchers attached an inflatable cuff at the connection between the stomach and the small intestine.","printedPages":[308],"pdfPages":[326],"kind":"textbook_selected_research","evidenceMethod":"single_verified_textbook_passage"},"classroomCoverage":{"status":"source_structured_full_book","level":"comprehensive_book_derived","topicHeadings":19,"bullets":64,"newWords":2688,"allTopicsWithExplanations":true,"sourceScope":"verified_pdf_topic_facts_crosschecked_with_uploaded_markdown"},"classroomFigures":[{"id":"figure-9-16","headingId":"bp14-m9-3-h07","number":"9.16","title":"Insulin and glucagon feedback","printedPage":309,"pdfPage":327,"alt":"Excerpt from Figure 9.16 of Kalat Biological Psychology, showing insulin and glucagon feedback.","image":"data:image/webp;base64,","width":496,"height":840,"source":"Cropped figure from user-supplied textbook PDF","cropPdfPoints":[69,326,317,746],"status":"figure number and printed page checked in PDF; crop visually reviewed by montage"}]},{"id":"bp14-m10-1","chapterId":"bp14-ch10","moduleId":"bp14-m10-1","moduleNumber":"10.1","title":"Sex and Hormones","kind":"detailed_source_grounded_notes","printedStart":324,"printedEnd":338,"pdfStart":342,"pdfEnd":356,"content":[{"type":"paragraph","text":"Sex-related development and behavior involve genes, hormones, and experience. Organizing hormonal effects during development differ from activating effects that operate later."},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The module discusses male–female differences, mate preferences, reproductive physiology, and parental behavior. Distinguish average group patterns from claims about any one individual, and keep proposed evolutionary accounts separate from evidence about mechanisms."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m10-1-study-1","text":"Sexual development occurs in stages"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Biological development of reproductive systems involves chromosomes, genes, gonadal development, hormones, receptors, and their timing. A simple picture in which one gene directly produces every male-typical or female-typical feature misses the developmental sequence. Hormones can have organizing effects that influence the development of tissues and neural circuits, particularly during sensitive periods. They can also have activating effects that alter behavior or physiology in a mature organism. These two kinds of influence should be distinguished clearly."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m10-1-study-2","text":"Hormones and variation"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Sex hormones influence body and brain development, but their effects depend on exposure, receptor sensitivity, and wider biological context. Some measured sex differences are statistical averages with large overlap among individuals. Traits are also influenced by experience, culture, and opportunities. Avoid drawing a straight line from a hormone level to a complex behavior, especially when evidence comes from animal studies or comparisons that do not control for environment."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m10-1-study-3","text":"Evolutionary ideas and mate preferences"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The module considers evolutionary interpretations of patterns such as preferences, jealousy, and mating strategies. An evolutionary account asks how a behavior may have influenced reproduction over generations. It must not be mistaken for a moral rule or the claim that every person follows the same pattern. A reported difference in average preferences is not a universal statement about what individuals want or ought to do. Interpret these hypotheses through the evidence presented, not stereotypes."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m10-1-study-4","text":"Parental behavior"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Parental care reflects interacting hormonal, neural, experiential, and social factors. Biological systems can facilitate responsiveness to offspring, but caregiving varies across individuals and circumstances. Sexual behavior, reproductive development, and parental behavior belong to related but distinct explanatory questions. Studying their mechanisms helps show why the phrase 'sex hormones' describes a range of influences rather than one narrow function."},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m10-1-h01","text":"Evolutionary Interpretations of Male–Female Differences"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"According to Charles Darwin’s theory of evolution by natural selection, individuals whose genes help them survive will produce more offspring, and therefore those genes will spread in the population.","sourcePrintedPage":324,"sourcePdfPage":342,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A second part of his theory was sexual selection : Genes that increase an individual’s probability of mating, or probable number of surviving offspring, will also spread in the population.","sourcePrintedPage":324,"sourcePdfPage":342,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In many bird species, the male’s brightly colored feathers are important for attracting females.","sourcePrintedPage":324,"sourcePdfPage":342,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In a few species, such as phalaropes, the female lays eggs and then deserts them, leaving the male to attend to them.","sourcePrintedPage":324,"sourcePdfPage":342,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In humans, too, some male–female differences may be results of sexual selection.","sourcePrintedPage":324,"sourcePdfPage":342,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m10-1-h02","text":"Interest in Multiple Mates"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Across cultures, more males than females seek opportunities for multiple sexual partners.","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The idea is that males in the past who acted in either of these ways propagated their genes.","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In contrast, a woman can have no more than one pregnancy per 9 months, regardless of her number of sex partners.","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A woman can sometimes gain from having multiple sex partners .","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If her partner is infertile, then mating with another man could be her only way of reproducing.","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In addition, she has the possibility of “trading up,” abandoning her first mate for a better one.","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Still, men potentially have more to gain from multiple sex partners than women do.","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers have no direct evidence that genes influence people’s preferences for one mate or many.","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, males of most other mammalian species also seek multiple mates, and their behavior is almost certainly genetically based.","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m10-1-h03","text":"Differences in Jealousy"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"An evolutionary standpoint suggests this explanation: For a male to pass on his genes, he should be sure that the children he supports are his own, and an unfaithful female threatens that certainty.","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because a female knows that any children she bears are her own, she does not have that worry, although she might worry if her partner starts supporting some other female’s children, instead of hers.","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Women reported that they would be more upset if their partner became emotionally intimate with another woman than if he had sex with her .","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Several similar studies have found similar results, although the size of the effect varies among cultures .","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The difference is not huge, because both men and women are upset about either sexual or emotional infidelity.","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, as was the case with preferences for multiple partners, we have no direct evidence of any gene that controls jealousy.","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Mate-guarding or sexual jealousy occurs in many other mammals, but it is not universal.","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m10-1-h04","text":"Mate Preferences"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A difference is that women are more likely than men to prefer a mate who is likely to be a good provider .","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Evolutionary theorists emphasize that while a woman is pregnant or taking care of a small child, she may need help with food and other requirements, and therefore evolution would have favored a tendency for women to seek good providers.","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The tendency for females to prefer good providers is mostly limited to humans, because most male mammals provide little help to pregnant or nursing females.","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If the preference for a good provider is a product of evolution, it had to be relatively recent, as evolution goes.","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m10-1-h05","text":"Genes in Sexual Development"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Females have two X chromosomes, whereas males have an X and a Y chromosome. (The mechanisms of sex determination differ for birds, reptiles, and fish.) Biologists used to believe that the chromosomes determine sexual differentiation entirely through hormones.","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"We will get to the hormones, but let’s start with effects of genes themselves.","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because males have only one X chromosome, a recessive gene on the X chromosome shows its effects more often in males than in females, including some effects that cause intellectual deficiencies .","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Turner syndrome is characterized by an XO pattern—an X chromosome and no second sex chromosome, or just part of a second X chromosome, or one X in some cells and two Xs in others.","sourcePrintedPage":326,"sourcePdfPage":344,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The result is a typical feminine appearance, and almost always self-identification as female, but ovaries that secrete less than average amounts of sex hormones.","sourcePrintedPage":326,"sourcePdfPage":344,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Klinefelter syndrome is characterized by an XXY pattern, or less commonly XXYY or XXXY.","sourcePrintedPage":326,"sourcePdfPage":344,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One research problem is that all these chromosomal anomalies are more likely to be noticed in people who are brought to medical attention because of physical or behavioral problems.","sourcePrintedPage":326,"sourcePdfPage":344,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m10-1-h06","text":"Organizing Effects of Sex Hormones"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A little later in biological males, the SRY gene (Sex-determining Region on the Y chromosome) causes those undifferentiated gonads to develop into testes , the sperm-producing organs.","sourcePrintedPage":326,"sourcePdfPage":344,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The testes also produce Müllerian-inhibiting hormone ( MIH ) that causes the Müllerian ducts to degenerate.","sourcePrintedPage":326,"sourcePdfPage":344,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because biological females do not have the SRY gene, the gonads develop into ovaries instead of testes, the Wolffian ducts degenerate, and the Müllerian ducts mature into oviducts, uterus, and the upper vagina.","sourcePrintedPage":326,"sourcePdfPage":344,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The males’ testes produce more androgens than estrogens (hormones that are more abundant in females), whereas the females’ ovaries produce more estrogens than androgens.","sourcePrintedPage":327,"sourcePdfPage":345,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The adrenal glands also produce smaller amounts of both androgens and estrogens, and the brain produces estrogens, which aid in memory and other cognitive functions .","sourcePrintedPage":327,"sourcePdfPage":345,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The surge of hormones at puberty produces breast development in females, facial hair and penis growth in males, and changes in voice .","sourcePrintedPage":327,"sourcePdfPage":345,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For example, organizing effects set up the female hypothalamus such that later hormones can activate the menstrual cycle.","sourcePrintedPage":328,"sourcePdfPage":346,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A high level of testosterone causes the external genitals to develop the male pattern, and a low level leads to the female pattern.","sourcePrintedPage":328,"sourcePdfPage":346,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In short, early testosterone promotes the male pattern and inhibits the female pattern .","sourcePrintedPage":329,"sourcePdfPage":347,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Injecting a genetic male with estrogens during early development produces little effect on his external anatomy, but a genetic male that lacks androgens or androgen receptors develops a female-typical pattern of anatomy and behavior.","sourcePrintedPage":329,"sourcePdfPage":347,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m10-1-h07","text":"Sex Differences in the Brain"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The female hypothalamus generates a cyclic pattern of hormone release, as in the human menstrual cycle, whereas the male hypothalamus releases hormones more steadily.","sourcePrintedPage":329,"sourcePdfPage":347,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Research by Margaret McCarthy and her colleagues has found that the mechanisms differ from one brain area to another.","sourcePrintedPage":330,"sourcePdfPage":348,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In part of the ventromedial hypothalamus, estradiol activates an enzyme called PI3 kinase that increases glutamate release, and thereby causes postsynaptic neurons to increase their dendritic branching .","sourcePrintedPage":330,"sourcePdfPage":348,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"These areas remain larger in females because of their relatively low levels of brain estradiol during early development .","sourcePrintedPage":330,"sourcePdfPage":348,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because the mechanisms differ from one brain area to another, it is possible for one area to become more masculinized or more feminized than another.","sourcePrintedPage":330,"sourcePdfPage":348,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In many brain areas, the male–female differences depend on not only testosterone and estradiol but also the immune system and genes that are more active in one sex or the other .","sourcePrintedPage":330,"sourcePdfPage":348,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because genes vary, and so do epigenetic changes, few people have a brain that is male-typical or female-typical in all regards.","sourcePrintedPage":330,"sourcePdfPage":348,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Brain anatomy is “nonbinary.” And just as it is true that brains are a mosaic of male-typical and female-typical areas, most people have a mixture of male-typical and female-typical interests, attitudes, and activities.","sourcePrintedPage":330,"sourcePdfPage":348,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m10-1-h08","text":"Sex Differences in Play"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The average difference between boys and girls in toy preference is bigger than the average difference between men and women in height .","sourcePrintedPage":331,"sourcePdfPage":349,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Boys more often choose to play with toy cars and trains, balls, guns, and roughhouse activities.","sourcePrintedPage":331,"sourcePdfPage":349,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Socialization contributes to the pattern, as most parents give their sons and daughters different sets of toys, but socialization need not be the whole story.","sourcePrintedPage":331,"sourcePdfPage":349,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Indeed, it may be that parents give those toys because previous generations observed differences in boys’ and girls’ interests.","sourcePrintedPage":331,"sourcePdfPage":349,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Other studies found that prenatal injections of testosterone to female monkey fetuses led to increased masculine-type play after they were born.","sourcePrintedPage":331,"sourcePdfPage":349,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In those cases, the focus was on spontaneous, rough-andtumble play rather than playing with toys, but the idea is similar .","sourcePrintedPage":331,"sourcePdfPage":349,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Back to humans: Researchers correlated chemicals in the mother’s blood during pregnancy with the daughters’ toy choices at age 31⁄2.","sourcePrintedPage":331,"sourcePdfPage":349,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"study measured testosterone in the amniotic fluid of 212 pregnant women and found a significant correlation with the male-typical play of their children 6 to 10 years later .","sourcePrintedPage":331,"sourcePdfPage":349,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Still another study measured testosterone levels in infants over the first 6 months and compared results to their toy choices at age 14 months.","sourcePrintedPage":331,"sourcePdfPage":349,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m10-1-h09","text":"Activating Effects of Sex Hormones"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"At any time in life, current levels of testosterone or estradiol exert activating effects, temporarily modifying behavior.","sourcePrintedPage":331,"sourcePdfPage":349,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For example, when doves court each other, each stage of their behavior initiates hormonal changes that alter the birds’ readiness for the next sequence of behaviors .","sourcePrintedPage":331,"sourcePdfPage":349,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In addition to the sex hormones, the pituitary hormone oxytocin is also important for reproductive behavior.","sourcePrintedPage":331,"sourcePdfPage":349,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Oxytocin stimulates contractions of the uterus during delivery of a baby, and it stimulates the mammary gland to release milk.","sourcePrintedPage":331,"sourcePdfPage":349,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Sexual pleasure releases oxytocin, especially at orgasm .","sourcePrintedPage":331,"sourcePdfPage":349,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Oxytocin is responsible for the calmness and reduced anxiety after orgasm .","sourcePrintedPage":331,"sourcePdfPage":349,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m10-1-h10","text":"Males"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Testosterone primes the medial preoptic area (MPOA) and other brain areas to release dopamine, which then increases male sex drive .","sourcePrintedPage":331,"sourcePdfPage":349,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In moderate concentrations, dopamine stimulates mostly type D 1 and D 5 receptors, which facilitate erection of the penis .","sourcePrintedPage":331,"sourcePdfPage":349,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Whereas dopamine stimulates sexual activity, the neurotransmitter serotonin inhibits it by blocking dopamine release .","sourcePrintedPage":332,"sourcePdfPage":350,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers found that, on average, married men and men living with a woman in a committed relationship have lower testosterone levels than unpaired men of the same age .","sourcePrintedPage":332,"sourcePdfPage":350,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Two explanations are possible: Marriage might decrease testosterone levels, because of decreased need to seek a sexual partner, or men with lower testosterone levels might be more likely to marry and remain faithful.","sourcePrintedPage":332,"sourcePdfPage":350,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, low testosterone is not the usual basis for impotence , the inability to have an erection.","sourcePrintedPage":332,"sourcePdfPage":350,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The drug sildenafil (Viagra) increases male sexual ability by increasing blood flow to the penis.","sourcePrintedPage":332,"sourcePdfPage":350,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m10-1-h11","text":"Females"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"After the end of a menstrual period, the anterior pituitary releases follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) , which promotes the growth of a follicle in the ovary.","sourcePrintedPage":332,"sourcePdfPage":350,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The follicle nurtures the ovum (egg cell) and produces several types of estrogen, including estradiol.","sourcePrintedPage":332,"sourcePdfPage":350,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The increased estradiol increases release of FSH and a surge in the release of luteinizing hormone (LH) from the anterior pituitary (the top graph in Figure 10.7).","sourcePrintedPage":332,"sourcePdfPage":350,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Note, however, that birth control pills do not protect against sexually transmitted diseases.","sourcePrintedPage":333,"sourcePdfPage":351,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Estradiol increases the sensitivity of the pudendal nerve , which transmits tactile stimulation from the vagina and cervix","sourcePrintedPage":333,"sourcePdfPage":351,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Just as testosterone facilitates dopamine release in the medial preoptic area for males, estradiol does the same for females .","sourcePrintedPage":333,"sourcePdfPage":351,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Most women report a decrease in sexual desire after menopause, which decreases estradiol levels, or after surgical removal of the ovaries, which also reduces estradiol levels .","sourcePrintedPage":333,"sourcePdfPage":351,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Furthermore, a study comparing women’s increases and decreases of sexual interest from day to day across one or two months found that sexual desire correlated strongly with changes in levels of estradiol, not testosterone .","sourcePrintedPage":333,"sourcePdfPage":351,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, her probability of initiating sexual activity does increase at that time (Figure 10.9).","sourcePrintedPage":334,"sourcePdfPage":352,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Another study used a method that is, shall we say, uncommon among laboratory researchers.","sourcePrintedPage":334,"sourcePdfPage":352,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The researchers studied erotic lap dancers, who earn tips by dancing between a man’s legs, rubbing up against his groin, while wearing, in most cases, just a bikini bottom.","sourcePrintedPage":334,"sourcePdfPage":352,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m10-1-h12","text":"Parental Behavior"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In male mammals that participate in care for the young, oxytocin is important for their parental behavior also .","sourcePrintedPage":334,"sourcePdfPage":352,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Late in pregnancy, sensitivity to estradiol increases in the brain areas important for maternal behavior and attention to the young , including the medial preoptic area and anterior hypothalamus and nucleus accumbens .","sourcePrintedPage":334,"sourcePdfPage":352,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"We have already encountered the preoptic area/anterior hypothalamus, or POA/AH, because of its importance for temperature regulation and thirst.","sourcePrintedPage":334,"sourcePdfPage":352,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Decreased brain volume sounds like a bad thing, but it is a result of pruning the most ineffective synapses.","sourcePrintedPage":334,"sourcePdfPage":352,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The brain areas that decrease volume during pregnancy are the areas that become most active when attending to the needs of a baby, and greater decreases in volume correlate with increased maternal attachment.","sourcePrintedPage":334,"sourcePdfPage":352,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, researchers found a way to increase activity of the genes responsible for vasopressin in the hypothalamus.","sourcePrintedPage":335,"sourcePdfPage":353,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Ordinarily, female rats ignore or avoid baby rats, mainly because of an aversion to their odor.","sourcePrintedPage":335,"sourcePdfPage":353,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When a female gives birth, the delivery causes a change in her brain that makes the infants’ odor more appealing .","sourcePrintedPage":335,"sourcePdfPage":353,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because the babies cannot survive without care, the experimenter periodically replaces them with new, healthy babies.","sourcePrintedPage":335,"sourcePdfPage":353,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"This process might seem like just a laboratory curiosity, but it is important in nature.","sourcePrintedPage":335,"sourcePdfPage":353,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Brain scans also indicate expansion of several areas in her brain from early to late pregnancy and then delivery, especially in areas responsible for reward and motivation.","sourcePrintedPage":336,"sourcePdfPage":354,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In most respects, however, human parental behavior is experience-dependent rather than hormone-dependent.","sourcePrintedPage":336,"sourcePdfPage":354,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m10-1-h13","text":"In Closing: Reproductive Behaviors and Motivations"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Each of us is a product of our upbringing, and also a product of chemical influences that began before birth and continued thereafter.","sourcePrintedPage":336,"sourcePdfPage":354,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"On average, men with lower testosterone levels and higher prolactin levels spend more time playing with and caring for their children .","sourcePrintedPage":336,"sourcePdfPage":354,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Over the next few months after a baby is born, the father’s testosterone level increases, and those with more rapid increases tend to contribute less to child care in some ways .","sourcePrintedPage":336,"sourcePdfPage":354,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because all of these are correlational data, we do not know to what extent the hormones are the cause of the men’s behavior, and to what extent they are the result.","sourcePrintedPage":336,"sourcePdfPage":354,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The presence or absence of testosterone determines whether a mammal will differentiate as a male or a female.","sourcePrintedPage":337,"sourcePdfPage":355,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"bullet","text":"In those species, the female’s bright colors help her attract a male.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h01","sourcePrintedPage":324,"sourcePdfPage":342},{"type":"bullet","text":"From the evolutionary standpoint of spreading one’s genes, males can succeed by either of two strategies: be loyal to one woman and devote your energies to helping her and her babies, or mate with many women and hope that some of them can raise your babies without your help.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h02","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343},{"type":"bullet","text":"Some cultures tolerate sexual infidelity by husbands but not wives, and some tolerate it by both or neither, but no known society considers infidelity more acceptable for women than for men.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h03","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343},{"type":"bullet","text":"David Buss and colleagues surveyed heterosexual young people and found, as they predicted, that men said they would be more upset if their partner became sexually intimate with another man than if she became emotionally intimate with him.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h03","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343},{"type":"bullet","text":"All this discussion is an attempt to explain how people usually do act, not to say how they should act.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h03","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343},{"type":"bullet","text":"The needs of life in a civilized society sometimes conflict with biological tendencies.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h03","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343},{"type":"bullet","text":"Almost everyone, regardless of gender or sexual orientation, prefers a romantic partner who is healthy, intelligent, honest, kind, and physically attractive, with religious and political beliefs similar to one’s own.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h04","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343},{"type":"bullet","text":"This evolutionary explanation is less persuasive than in the previous two examples.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h04","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343},{"type":"bullet","text":"Furthermore, in countries where women have good economic opportunities of their own, their preference for a wealthy male is substantially weaker.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h04","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343},{"type":"bullet","text":"A few genes on the Y chromosome are active in the brain, at least one gene on the X chromosome is active only in the female brain, and several genes on the X chromosome produce larger effects in females.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h05","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343},{"type":"bullet","text":"The X and Y chromosomes also have sites that alter the expression of genes on other chromosomes.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h05","sourcePrintedPage":325,"sourcePdfPage":343},{"type":"bullet","text":"Most women with Turner syndrome are shorter than average and few have successful pregnancies without medical help.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h05","sourcePrintedPage":326,"sourcePdfPage":344},{"type":"bullet","text":"A common pattern is below average math and visuospatial skills, but normal or above-average performance on certain aspects of language.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h05","sourcePrintedPage":326,"sourcePdfPage":344},{"type":"bullet","text":"The testes are smaller than average, and some breast growth is common at puberty.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h05","sourcePrintedPage":326,"sourcePdfPage":344},{"type":"bullet","text":"Learning difficulties are common, especially with language and problem solving, and mental health problems are elevated.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h05","sourcePrintedPage":326,"sourcePdfPage":344},{"type":"bullet","text":"Male and female mammals have the same anatomy during an early stage of prenatal development.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h06","sourcePrintedPage":326,"sourcePdfPage":344},{"type":"bullet","text":"The testes produce androgens (male-typical hormones) that increase the growth of the testes, causing them to produce still more androgens.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h06","sourcePrintedPage":326,"sourcePdfPage":344},{"type":"bullet","text":"Androgens and estrogens have similar effects in some ways and different effects in others.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h06","sourcePrintedPage":327,"sourcePdfPage":345},{"type":"bullet","text":"The results depend on the species and the duration of exposure, but in general the behavioral effects are unimpressive.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h06","sourcePrintedPage":327,"sourcePdfPage":345},{"type":"bullet","text":"The anatomical changes at puberty persist throughout life, even after the concentration of sex hormones declines.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h06","sourcePrintedPage":327,"sourcePdfPage":345},{"type":"bullet","text":"For example, current hormone levels influence the degree of sex drive.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h06","sourcePrintedPage":327,"sourcePdfPage":345},{"type":"bullet","text":"The distinction between organizing and activating effects is not absolute, as hormones often produce a combination of temporary and longer-lasting effects (Arnold and Breedlove, 1985; C.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h06","sourcePrintedPage":328,"sourcePdfPage":346},{"type":"bullet","text":"Let’s focus on the organizing effects during the early sensitive period, when hormones determine whether an embryo develops a male or female anatomy.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h06","sourcePrintedPage":328,"sourcePdfPage":346},{"type":"bullet","text":"Estradiol is essential for proper development of a female’s uterus and other internal organs, but it has little effect on the external genitals.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h06","sourcePrintedPage":328,"sourcePdfPage":346},{"type":"bullet","text":"For the rest of the brain, male and female brains differ on average in many ways, although the differences are small, and definitely “on average,” with a full overlap between the male and female distributions.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h07","sourcePrintedPage":329,"sourcePdfPage":347},{"type":"bullet","text":"The illustration shows which brain areas tend to form a larger percentage of the male brain or the female brain.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h07","sourcePrintedPage":329,"sourcePdfPage":347},{"type":"bullet","text":"In rats during early development, a male’s testosterone enters cells of the hypothalamus, where an enzyme converts much of it to estradiol, which exerts masculinizing effects at this time.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h07","sourcePrintedPage":330,"sourcePdfPage":348},{"type":"bullet","text":"In the medial preoptic area, both testosterone itself and its conversion to estradiol increase the production of a chemical called prostaglandin E 2, which leads to an increase in microglia, dendritic spines, and synapses.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h07","sourcePrintedPage":330,"sourcePdfPage":348},{"type":"bullet","text":"In humans and other primates, testosterone acts on the hypothalamus directly instead of by conversion to estradiol, but the final mechanism in terms of prostaglandins, PI3 kinase, and so forth appear to be the same as in rodents.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h07","sourcePrintedPage":330,"sourcePdfPage":348},{"type":"bullet","text":"One of the larger male–female differences in behavior relates to play.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h08","sourcePrintedPage":331,"sourcePdfPage":349},{"type":"bullet","text":"Children who show the most boy-typical play at age 3 usually show the greatest preference for boy-typical activities at age 13, and those with the most girl-typical play at 3 usually show the greatest preference for girl-typical activities at 13.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h08","sourcePrintedPage":331,"sourcePdfPage":349},{"type":"bullet","text":"Girls with higher testosterone levels in early infancy spent more time than average playing with toy trains, compared to other girls.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h08","sourcePrintedPage":331,"sourcePdfPage":349},{"type":"bullet","text":"Androgens, essential for male sexual arousal, increase sensitivity in the penis and bind to receptors in the hypothalamus.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h10","sourcePrintedPage":331,"sourcePdfPage":349},{"type":"bullet","text":"In rats, a few minutes of exposure to a receptive female also releases dopamine in the MPOA, producing the same effect.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h10","sourcePrintedPage":331,"sourcePdfPage":349},{"type":"bullet","text":"Many antidepressant drugs increase serotonin activity, and one of their side effects is decreased sexual arousal.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h10","sourcePrintedPage":332,"sourcePdfPage":350},{"type":"bullet","text":"For example, castration decreases a man’s sexual interest and activity.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h10","sourcePrintedPage":332,"sourcePdfPage":350},{"type":"bullet","text":"A woman’s hypothalamus and pituitary interact with the ovaries to produce the menstrual cycle, a periodic variation in hormones and fertility over the course of about 28 days.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h11","sourcePrintedPage":332,"sourcePdfPage":350},{"type":"bullet","text":"Toward the middle of the menstrual cycle, the follicle builds up more and more receptors to FSH, so that even though the concentration of FSH in the blood is decreasing, its effects on the follicle increase.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h11","sourcePrintedPage":332,"sourcePdfPage":350},{"type":"bullet","text":"The remnant of the follicle (now called the corpus luteum ) releases the hormone progesterone, which prepares the uterus for the implantation of a fertilized ovum.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h11","sourcePrintedPage":332,"sourcePdfPage":350},{"type":"bullet","text":"Otherwise, both hormones decline (as shown in Figure 10.7), the lining of the uterus is cast off (menstruation), and the cycle begins again.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h11","sourcePrintedPage":332,"sourcePdfPage":350},{"type":"bullet","text":"Increased sensitivity to nausea may be an evolved adaptation to minimize the risk of eating something harmful to the fetus.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h11","sourcePrintedPage":333,"sourcePdfPage":351},{"type":"bullet","text":"Birth control pills prevent pregnancy by interfering with the usual feedback cycle between the ovaries and the pituitary.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h11","sourcePrintedPage":333,"sourcePdfPage":351},{"type":"bullet","text":"Estradiol appears to be essential to female sexual behavior in all mammals that have been tested.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h11","sourcePrintedPage":333,"sourcePdfPage":351},{"type":"bullet","text":"At one time, the idea arose that human female sexual desire might depend on testosterone.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h11","sourcePrintedPage":333,"sourcePdfPage":351},{"type":"bullet","text":"After she delivers the young, she increases her secretion of oxytocin and prolactin, which promote milk production and several aspects of maternal behavior.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h12","sourcePrintedPage":334,"sourcePdfPage":352},{"type":"bullet","text":"In humans, it has been demonstrated that pregnancy leads to decreased gray matter volume in several brain areas, as in Figure 10.10.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h12","sourcePrintedPage":334,"sourcePdfPage":352},{"type":"bullet","text":"The hormone vasopressin is important for social behavior in many species.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h12","sourcePrintedPage":335,"sourcePdfPage":353},{"type":"bullet","text":"Male prairie voles, which secrete much vasopressin, establish long-term pair bonds with females and help rear their young.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h12","sourcePrintedPage":335,"sourcePdfPage":353},{"type":"bullet","text":"In humans, researchers have reported that men with genes for less-active forms of the vasopressin receptor are less likely to marry, more likely to have marital conflicts or threat of divorce, and in general less likely to show altruistic behavior toward others.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h12","sourcePrintedPage":335,"sourcePdfPage":353},{"type":"bullet","text":"(Without giving birth, she does not secrete the prolactin and oxytocin necessary for milk production.) This experience-dependent behavior does not require hormonal changes and occurs even in females that had their ovaries removed.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h12","sourcePrintedPage":335,"sourcePdfPage":353},{"type":"bullet","text":"Several studies have reported a correlation between fathers’ hormones and their behavior toward their infants and toddlers.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h12","sourcePrintedPage":336,"sourcePdfPage":354},{"type":"bullet","text":"You can make a voluntary decision about how to handle your sexual motivations, but the motivations themselves have a biological basis.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h13","sourcePrintedPage":336,"sourcePdfPage":354},{"type":"bullet","text":"In birds, the story is the opposite: The presence or absence of estrogen is critical.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h13","sourcePrintedPage":337,"sourcePdfPage":355},{"type":"bullet","text":"(Hint: Think about the difference between live birth and hatching from an egg.) 2.","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h13","sourcePrintedPage":337,"sourcePdfPage":355}],"topicIds":["bp14-m10-1-h01","bp14-m10-1-h02","bp14-m10-1-h03","bp14-m10-1-h04","bp14-m10-1-h05","bp14-m10-1-h06","bp14-m10-1-h07","bp14-m10-1-h08","bp14-m10-1-h09","bp14-m10-1-h10","bp14-m10-1-h11","bp14-m10-1-h12","bp14-m10-1-h13"],"studySections":[{"id":"bp14-m10-1-study-1","title":"Sexual development occurs in stages","text":"Biological development of reproductive systems involves chromosomes, genes, gonadal development, hormones, receptors, and their timing. .","printedPage":325,"pdfPage":343,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":42},{"text":"Turner syndrome is characterized by an XO pattern—an X chromosome own, she does not have that worry, although she might worry if her partner starts supporting some other female’s children, instead of hers.","printedPage":325,"pdfPage":343,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":28},{"text":"Women reported that they would be more upset if their partner became emotionally intimate with another woman than if he had sex with her .","printedPage":325,"pdfPage":343,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":29},{"text":"Several similar studies have found similar results, although the size of the effect varies among cultures .","printedPage":325,"pdfPage":343,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":30},{"text":"The difference is not huge, because both men and women are upset about either sexual or emotional infidelity.","printedPage":325,"pdfPage":343,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":31},{"text":"However, as was the case with preferences for multiple partners, we have no direct evidence of any gene that controls jealousy.","printedPage":325,"pdfPage":343,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":32},{"text":"Mate-guarding or sexual jealousy occurs in many other mammals, but it is not universal.","printedPage":325,"pdfPage":343,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":33},{"text":"Some cultures tolerate sexual infidelity by husbands but not wives, and some tolerate it by both or neither, but no known society considers infidelity more acceptable for women than for men.","printedPage":325,"pdfPage":343,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":125},{"text":"David Buss and colleagues surveyed heterosexual young people and found, as they predicted, that men said they would be more upset if their partner became sexually intimate with another man than if she became emotionally intimate with him.","printedPage":325,"pdfPage":343,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":126},{"text":"All this discussion is an attempt to explain how people usually do act, not to say how they should act.","printedPage":325,"pdfPage":343,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":127},{"text":"The needs of life in a civilized society sometimes conflict with biological tendencies.","printedPage":325,"pdfPage":343,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":128}],"originalFacts":7,"additionalFacts":4,"glossary":[],"sourceBodyWordsAvailable":303,"sourceStatus":"source_explained","mdCrosscheck":"terms_present","wordCount":264},{"id":"bp14-m10-1-h04","title":"Mate provider .","printedPage":325,"pdfPage":343,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":35},{"text":"Evolutionary theorists emphasize that while a woman is providers.","printedPage":325,"pdfPage":343,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":36},{"text":"The tendency for females to prefer good providers is mostly limited to humans, because most male mammals provide little help to pregnant or nursing females.","printedPage":325,"pdfPage":343,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":37},{"text":"If the preference for a good provider is a product of evolution, it had to be relatively recent, as evolution goes.","printedPage":325,"pdfPage":343,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":38},{"text":"Almost everyone, regardless of gender or sexual orientation, prefers a romantic partner who is healthy, intelligent, honest, kind, and physically attractive, with religious and political beliefs similar to one’s own.","printedPage":325,"pdfPage":343,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":129},{"text":"This evolutionary explanation is less persuasive than in the previous two examples.","printedPage":325,"pdfPage":343,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":130},{"text":"Furthermore, in countries where women have good economic opportunities of their own, their preference for a wealthy male is substantially weaker.","printedPage":325,"pdfPage":343,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":131}],"originalFacts":4,"additionalFacts":3,"glossary":[{"term":"Evolutionary .","printedPage":325,"pdfPage":343,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":42},{"text":"Turner syndrome is characterized by an XO pattern—an X chromosome females.","printedPage":325,"pdfPage":343,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":132},{"text":"The X and Y chromosomes also have sites that alter the help.","printedPage":326,"pdfPage":344,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":134},{"text":"A common pattern is below average math and visuospatial skills, but normal or above-average performance on certain aspects of language.","printedPage":326,"pdfPage":344,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":135},{"text":"The testes are smaller than average, and some breast especially with language and problem solving, and mental health problems are .","printedPage":327,"pdfPage":345,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":52},{"text":"The surge of hormones at puberty produces breast development in .","printedPage":327,"pdfPage":345,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":53},{"text":"For example, organizing effects set up the female hypothalamus such species and the duration of exposure, but in general the behavioral effects are In most respects, however, human parental behavior is experience-dependent rather than hormone-dependent.","paragraphIndex":20070,"printedPages":[336]}],"status":"whole_book_source_structured_classroom_notes","basis":"uploaded_textbook_pdf_and_markdown","evidenceMethod":"source_heading_facts","sourceFactCount":12,"editorialVerification":"source-aligned, individual paraphrase review pending","followUpExplanation":"Late in pregnancy, sensitivity to estradiol increases in the brain areas important for maternal behavior and attention to the young, including the medial preoptic area and anterior hypothalamus and nucleus accumbens.","followUpParagraphIndex":20064},{"headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h13","title":"In Closing: Reproductive Behaviors and Motivations","level":1,"parentId":null,"printedPage":336,"pdfPage":354,"explanation":"Each of us is a product of our upbringing, and also a product of chemical influences that began before birth and continued thereafter.","paragraphIndex":20071,"bullets":[{"label":"Over the next few months after a baby","explanation":"Over the next few months after a baby is born, the father’s testosterone level increases, and those with more rapid increases tend to contribute less to child care in some ways. Because all of these are correlational data, we do not know to what extent the hormones are the cause of the men’s behavior, and to what extent they are the result.","paragraphIndex":20073,"printedPages":[336]},{"label":"Important detail","explanation":"The presence or absence of testosterone determines whether a mammal will differentiate as a male or a female.","paragraphIndex":20074,"printedPages":[337]}],"status":"whole_book_source_structured_classroom_notes","basis":"uploaded_textbook_pdf_and_markdown","evidenceMethod":"source_heading_facts","sourceFactCount":5,"editorialVerification":"source-aligned, individual paraphrase review pending","followUpExplanation":"On average, men with lower testosterone levels and higher prolactin levels spend more time playing with and caring for their children.","followUpParagraphIndex":20072}],"classroomParagraphs":["According to Charles Darwin’s theory of evolution by natural selection, individuals whose genes help them survive will produce more offspring, and therefore those genes will spread in the population.","A second part of his theory was sexual selection: Genes that increase an individual’s probability of mating, or probable number of surviving offspring, will also spread in the population.","In many bird species, the male’s brightly colored feathers are important for attracting females. In a few species, such as phalaropes, the female lays eggs and then deserts them, leaving the male to attend to them.","In humans, too, some male–female differences may be results of sexual selection.","Across cultures, more males than females seek opportunities for multiple sexual partners.","The idea is that males in the past who acted in either of these ways propagated their genes.","In contrast, a woman can have no more than one pregnancy per 9 months, regardless of her number of sex partners.","A woman can sometimes gain from having multiple sex partners. If her partner is infertile, then mating with another man could be her only way of reproducing.","In addition, she has the possibility of “trading up,” abandoning her first mate for a better one.","Still, men potentially have more to gain from multiple sex partners than women do. Researchers have no direct evidence that genes influence people’s preferences for one mate or many.","However, males of most other mammalian species also seek multiple mates, and their behavior is almost certainly genetically based.","An evolutionary standpoint suggests this explanation: For a male to pass on his genes, he should be sure that the children he supports are his own, and an unfaithful female threatens that certainty.","Because a female knows that any children she bears are her own, she does not have that worry, although she might worry if her partner starts supporting some other female’s children, instead of hers.","Women reported that they would be more upset if their partner became emotionally intimate with another woman than if he had sex with her. Several similar studies have found similar results, although the size of the effect varies among cultures.","The difference is not huge, because both men and women are upset about either sexual or emotional infidelity.","However, as was the case with preferences for multiple partners, we have no direct evidence of any gene that controls jealousy. Mate-guarding or sexual jealousy occurs in many other mammals, but it is not universal.","A difference is that women are more likely than men to prefer a mate who is likely to be a good provider.","Evolutionary theorists emphasize that while a woman is pregnant or taking care of a small child, she may need help with food and other requirements, and therefore evolution would have favored a tendency for women to seek good providers. The tendency for females to prefer good providers is mostly limited to humans, because most male mammals provide little help to pregnant or nursing females.","If the preference for a good provider is a product of evolution, it had to be relatively recent, as evolution goes.","Females have two X chromosomes, whereas males have an X and a Y chromosome. (The mechanisms of sex determination differ for birds, reptiles, and fish.) Biologists used to believe that the chromosomes determine sexual differentiation entirely through hormones.","We will get to the hormones, but let’s start with effects of genes themselves.","Because males have only one X chromosome, a recessive gene on the X chromosome shows its effects more often in males than in females, including some effects that cause intellectual deficiencies. Turner syndrome is characterized by an XO pattern—an X chromosome and no second sex chromosome, or just part of a second X chromosome, or one X in some cells and two Xs in others.","The result is a typical feminine appearance, and almost always self-identification as female, but ovaries that secrete less than average amounts of sex hormones.","Klinefelter syndrome is characterized by an XXY pattern, or less commonly XXYY or XXXY. One research problem is that all these chromosomal anomalies are more likely to be noticed in people who are brought to medical attention because of physical or behavioral problems.","A little later in biological males, the SRY gene (Sex-determining Region on the Y chromosome) causes those undifferentiated gonads to develop into testes, the sperm-producing organs.","The testes also produce Müllerian-inhibiting hormone ( MIH ) that causes the Müllerian ducts to degenerate.","Because biological females do not have the SRY gene, the gonads develop into ovaries instead of testes, the Wolffian ducts degenerate, and the Müllerian ducts mature into oviducts, uterus, and the upper vagina.","The males’ testes produce more androgens than estrogens (hormones that are more abundant in females), whereas the females’ ovaries produce more estrogens than androgens. The adrenal glands also produce smaller amounts of both androgens and estrogens, and the brain produces estrogens, which aid in memory and other cognitive functions.","The surge of hormones at puberty produces breast development in females, facial hair and penis growth in males, and changes in voice.","For example, organizing effects set up the female hypothalamus such that later hormones can activate the menstrual cycle.","A high level of testosterone causes the external genitals to develop the male pattern, and a low level leads to the female pattern. In short, early testosterone promotes the male pattern and inhibits the female pattern.","Injecting a genetic male with estrogens during early development produces little effect on his external anatomy, but a genetic male that lacks androgens or androgen receptors develops a female-typical pattern of anatomy and behavior.","The female hypothalamus generates a cyclic pattern of hormone release, as in the human menstrual cycle, whereas the male hypothalamus releases hormones more steadily.","Research by Margaret McCarthy and her colleagues has found that the mechanisms differ from one brain area to another.","In part of the ventromedial hypothalamus, estradiol activates an enzyme called PI3 kinase that increases glutamate release, and thereby causes postsynaptic neurons to increase their dendritic branching. These areas remain larger in females because of their relatively low levels of brain estradiol during early development.","Because the mechanisms differ from one brain area to another, it is possible for one area to become more masculinized or more feminized than another.","In many brain areas, the male–female differences depend on not only testosterone and estradiol but also the immune system and genes that are more active in one sex or the other.","Because genes vary, and so do epigenetic changes, few people have a brain that is male-typical or female-typical in all regards. Brain anatomy is “nonbinary.” And just as it is true that brains are a mosaic of male-typical and female-typical areas, most people have a mixture of male-typical and female-typical interests, attitudes, and activities.","The average difference between boys and girls in toy preference is bigger than the average difference between men and women in height.","Boys more often choose to play with toy cars and trains, balls, guns, and roughhouse activities.","Socialization contributes to the pattern, as most parents give their sons and daughters different sets of toys, but socialization need not be the whole story.","Indeed, it may be that parents give those toys because previous generations observed differences in boys’ and girls’ interests. Other studies found that prenatal injections of testosterone to female monkey fetuses led to increased masculine-type play after they were born.","In those cases, the focus was on spontaneous, rough-andtumble play rather than playing with toys, but the idea is similar.","Back to humans: Researchers correlated chemicals in the mother’s blood during pregnancy with the daughters’ toy choices at age 31⁄2. study measured testosterone in the amniotic fluid of 212 pregnant women and found a significant correlation with the male-typical play of their children 6 to 10 years later.","Still another study measured testosterone levels in infants over the first 6 months and compared results to their toy choices at age 14 months.","At any time in life, current levels of testosterone or estradiol exert activating effects, temporarily modifying behavior.","For example, when doves court each other, each stage of their behavior initiates hormonal changes that alter the birds’ readiness for the next sequence of behaviors.","In addition to the sex hormones, the pituitary hormone oxytocin is also important for reproductive behavior.","Oxytocin stimulates contractions of the uterus during delivery of a baby, and it stimulates the mammary gland to release milk. Sexual pleasure releases oxytocin, especially at orgasm.","Oxytocin is responsible for the calmness and reduced anxiety after orgasm.","Testosterone primes the medial preoptic area (MPOA) and other brain areas to release dopamine, which then increases male sex drive.","In moderate concentrations, dopamine stimulates mostly type D 1 and D 5 receptors, which facilitate erection of the penis.","Whereas dopamine stimulates sexual activity, the neurotransmitter serotonin inhibits it by blocking dopamine release. Researchers found that, on average, married men and men living with a woman in a committed relationship have lower testosterone levels than unpaired men of the same age.","Two explanations are possible: Marriage might decrease testosterone levels, because of decreased need to seek a sexual partner, or men with lower testosterone levels might be more likely to marry and remain faithful.","However, low testosterone is not the usual basis for impotence, the inability to have an erection. The drug sildenafil (Viagra) increases male sexual ability by increasing blood flow to the penis.","After the end of a menstrual period, the anterior pituitary releases follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), which promotes the growth of a follicle in the ovary.","The follicle nurtures the ovum (egg cell) and produces several types of estrogen, including estradiol.","The increased estradiol increases release of FSH and a surge in the release of luteinizing hormone (LH) from the anterior pituitary (the top graph in Figure 10.7). Note, however, that birth control pills do not protect against sexually transmitted diseases.","Estradiol increases the sensitivity of the pudendal nerve, which transmits tactile stimulation from the vagina and cervix","Just as testosterone facilitates dopamine release in the medial preoptic area for males, estradiol does the same for females.","Most women report a decrease in sexual desire after menopause, which decreases estradiol levels, or after surgical removal of the ovaries, which also reduces estradiol levels. Furthermore, a study comparing women’s increases and decreases of sexual interest from day to day across one or two months found that sexual desire correlated strongly with changes in levels of estradiol, not testosterone.","However, her probability of initiating sexual activity does increase at that time (Figure 10.9). Another study used a method that is, shall we say, uncommon among laboratory researchers.","The researchers studied erotic lap dancers, who earn tips by dancing between a man’s legs, rubbing up against his groin, while wearing, in most cases, just a bikini bottom.","In male mammals that participate in care for the young, oxytocin is important for their parental behavior also.","Late in pregnancy, sensitivity to estradiol increases in the brain areas important for maternal behavior and attention to the young, including the medial preoptic area and anterior hypothalamus and nucleus accumbens.","We have already encountered the preoptic area/anterior hypothalamus, or POA/AH, because of its importance for temperature regulation and thirst. Decreased brain volume sounds like a bad thing, but it is a result of pruning the most ineffective synapses.","The brain areas that decrease volume during pregnancy are the areas that become most active when attending to the needs of a baby, and greater decreases in volume correlate with increased maternal attachment.","However, researchers found a way to increase activity of the genes responsible for vasopressin in the hypothalamus. Ordinarily, female rats ignore or avoid baby rats, mainly because of an aversion to their odor.","When a female gives birth, the delivery causes a change in her brain that makes the infants’ odor more appealing. Because the babies cannot survive without care, the experimenter periodically replaces them with new, healthy babies.","This process might seem like just a laboratory curiosity, but it is important in nature.","Brain scans also indicate expansion of several areas in her brain from early to late pregnancy and then delivery, especially in areas responsible for reward and motivation. In most respects, however, human parental behavior is experience-dependent rather than hormone-dependent.","Each of us is a product of our upbringing, and also a product of chemical influences that began before birth and continued thereafter.","On average, men with lower testosterone levels and higher prolactin levels spend more time playing with and caring for their children.","Over the next few months after a baby is born, the father’s testosterone level increases, and those with more rapid increases tend to contribute less to child care in some ways. Because all of these are correlational data, we do not know to what extent the hormones are the cause of the men’s behavior, and to what extent they are the result.","The presence or absence of testosterone determines whether a mammal will differentiate as a male or a female."],"classroomResearch":{"title":"Evidence in context: Males","body":"Researchers found that, on average, married men and men living with a woman in a committed relationship have lower testosterone levels than unpaired men of the same age.","printedPages":[332],"pdfPages":[350],"kind":"textbook_selected_research","evidenceMethod":"single_verified_textbook_passage"},"classroomCoverage":{"status":"source_structured_full_book","level":"comprehensive_book_derived","topicHeadings":13,"bullets":50,"newWords":2168,"allTopicsWithExplanations":true,"sourceScope":"verified_pdf_topic_facts_crosschecked_with_uploaded_markdown"},"classroomFigures":[{"id":"figure-10-1","headingId":"bp14-m10-1-h05","number":"10.1","title":"Differentiation of human genitals","printedPage":326,"pdfPage":344,"alt":"Excerpt from Figure 10.1 of Kalat Biological Psychology, showing differentiation of human genitals.","image":"data:image/webp;base64,
